comment: Line 814 and Table 3.5 enumerate SNOMED CT (and SNOMED GPS), ICD-11, and LOINC as required terminology standards. The document is silent on cross-maps between these standards, specifically the SNOMED CT to ICD-11 MMS map and the SNOMED CT-LOINC alignment. These cross-maps are operationally essential: a country using SNOMED CT for clinical data capture must map to ICD-11 MMS for administrative and statistical reporting. Without authoritative cross-maps, countries will build their own divergent, unmaintained mappings or fail to meet both requirements simultaneously. Historically, SNOMED International and WHO have collaborated on an official SNOMED CT-ICD 10 map; SNOMED International and Regenstrief collaborate on SNOMED CT-LOINC alignment via the LOINC Ontology. These resources are precisely what implementing countries will need.

public.suggestedRevision: We suggest the authors add to section 3.4.5 or Table 3.5: "Cross-maps between SNOMED CT, ICD-11 MMS, and LOINC are a required component of a functional national Terminology Service, not an optional enhancement. WHO and ITU should commission a joint Mapping Governance White Paper, co-authored with SNOMED International, WHO's ICD-11 programme, and Regenstrief Institute, providing countries with authoritative guidance on deploying and maintaining cross-terminology maps within their national SGI. Official SNOMED CT-ICD 10 maps are available from SNOMED International; and the LOINC Ontology from Regenstrief and SNOMED International jointly."
